doc.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sahara and the koto
summary: Tyner explains he brought a koto back from Japan and used it on Sahara.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: So a very fruitful relationship, so I noticed that during this time with Milestone and working with Orrin seems to be a blossoming in a lot of different directions so we already see that you're going into orchestration in 1967 and this really gets developed in your tenure with Milestone, so let’s look at this chronologically starting with Sahara. We talked earlier, I think Aisha mentioned, yeah you played Koto so I’m going to be interested in that, so how did that come about? Was that your suggestion or was that Orrin?
Well I’ve been to Japan and I brought a Koto back with me, we have it in the living room; we still have it right?

I like the sound of it. It was considered the Japanese piano before they started making pianos themselves. I enjoyed it, and I heard a lot of it when I was in Japan, so it was fascinating. Fooling around with it, I would pluck it. I didn’t study the instrument so I couldn’t say I was going to play it. I use it on some recordings on the intro. Anyway, it was very fruitful experimenting with different things.
